answer.rationale: Primary contract ends in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% and zero buffer, so stockout risk dominates TCO. memory_c1 is the load-bearing continuity claim for renewal (no migration, deliveries held). A low-cost primary switch (memory_c2) would chase the 18% spend cut but is treated as increasing delivery risk under these constraints; onboarding speed last year is not evidence it can cut over in two weeks with no buffer. Adding a second source (memory_c3) does not replace the expiring primary. Deferral (memory_c5) applied to a non-critical month-to-month case and is not assumed available here. Incumbent already refused to reopen price, so negotiate_terms is unlikely this cycle. Flagging downstream line-idle risk; not assuming unstated month-to-month or 14-day switch feasibility.
